newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U launches inhaler as aid to stop smoking.
newsitem.headline: P&U launches inhaler as aid to stop smoking.

text.p: U.S.-Swedish drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn (P&U) on Friday announced it was adding another product to its list of aids to help people stop smoking -- a Nicorette inhalor shaped like a mini-cigar.
The company said the inhalor was to be launched initially in Denmark on September 18 but the release would be quickly followed up in other European countries and worldwide.
"The Nicorette Inhalator will be our next big product that is designed to help people live without cigarettes," said P&U spokesman Arne Nordstrom in a statement.
The Nicorette inhaler is based on the same principles as the company's Nicorette chewing gum, patches and nasal spray.
A company spokeswoman said the inhalor was like a pen, but with the thickness of a small cigar and a flat mouthpiece.
The user puts a cartridge in the inhalor and can puff on it a few times to get nicotine.
"It is a nicotine impregnated plug and when you inhale the air becomes saturated by the vaporised nicotine," spokeswoman Christina Falk told Reuters.
"But as well as the nicotine, you get the behavioural effect," she added.
Falk said P&U had already got approval to launch the inhalor in Italy and the Netherlands and expected to release the project there early next year.
It was currently seeking approval in a few other countries including Sweden, the U.S. and all the major markets in Europe.
P&U said the inhalor had taken several years to develop and had been through six clinical studies with 1,440 smokers in Denmark, Sweden, and the U.S..
